name: The Delivery Rider Heir
blurb: Mocked by his ex at a rich party, a delivery rider takes a call that changes everything
title: The Delivery Rider Heir: Short Drama Script (Episode 1)
description: A free 2.5-minute vertical short drama script for 4 actors. A delivery rider is mocked by his ex at a luxury party, then a phone call flips the room.
h1: The Delivery Rider Heir: a 2.5-Minute Hidden Identity Short Drama Script, Episode 1
logline: Jay delivers twelve boxes of dumplings to a glittering party and finds his ex on the other side of the door. Her new boyfriend turns him into the evening's joke, until a call from a lawyer reveals why Jay has spent a year on a scooter.
setting: A party room (any living room with fairy lights) and the street outside. Props: a delivery jacket, helmet and thermal bag, takeaway boxes, a coin, two phones, a scooter or bicycle.

roles.name: Jay
roles.note: Mid 20s, a delivery rider finishing a secret year living on his own wages; calm, dry, hard to provoke.

roles.name: Sophie
roles.note: Mid 20s, Jay's ex; not cruel, but she judged him by his job.

roles.name: Marcus
roles.note: Late 20s, Sophie's showy boyfriend; loves an audience, crumbles under pressure.

roles.name: Ms. Reyes
roles.note: Any age 30 to 60, the family lawyer, heard on the phone; crisp and unshakeable. Any gender.

script.action: Music, fairy lights, people in evening clothes. JAY, mid twenties, in a delivery jacket and helmet, holds a thermal bag. The door is opened by SOPHIE, mid twenties, in a sparkling dress. Her smile dies.

script.say: Of all the doors in this city, you deliver to mine?
Twelve boxes of dumplings for Marcus. Order paid.

script.action: MARCUS, late twenties, in a velvet jacket, strolls over and puts an arm around Sophie.

script.say: Wait. Is this him? The ex?
Marcus, don't.
Everyone! This is the guy Sophie dumped two years ago. Look how well he's doing.

script.action: Guests laugh and lift their phones. Jay sets the boxes on a side table, unbothered.

script.say: Here. A tip.
script.how: dropping a coin into the empty bag

script.say: Save up. Maybe one day you'll be the one at the party instead of the one holding the bag.
You could have been something, Jay. You just never wanted it enough.
I wanted it exactly enough.

script.action: Jay's phone rings. He glances at it, and for the first time looks surprised. He answers.

script.say: Mr. Hart? It's Reyes. Your grandfather's year is over. Tonight at midnight, you'll have lived three hundred and sixty-five days on your own wages. The board is waiting for your answer.
One more delivery, then I'll call them.
There's something else. You're in the Marble Room on the twelfth floor?
How do you know that?
Because the building is ours, sir. And Marcus Bell's father is downstairs right now, asking our bank for a very large loan.

script.action: Jay lowers the phone. Across the room, Marcus's phone buzzes. He answers, still grinning. The grin disappears.

script.say: Dad? What do you mean, a delivery rider called Jay Hart? ... He's here. He's... standing right here.

script.action: Marcus turns to Jay, very pale. The room goes quiet. Phones lower.

script.say: Mr. Hart. That was a joke. The coin. A joke, obviously.

script.action: Jay takes the coin out of his bag and places it gently in Marcus's top pocket.

script.say: Keep it. You might need it tomorrow.

script.action: He picks up his helmet and walks to the door. Sophie runs after him.

script.say: Jay, wait. I didn't know. If I'd known who you were...
That's the problem, Sophie. You'd have stayed.

script.action: Jay pulls on his helmet beside a scooter. His phone rings again. Reyes.

script.say: Sir, one more thing. Your grandfather's will names a second heir. Someone you know.
Who?
Sophie Grant.

script.action: Jay turns slowly to look back at the building.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16. For the party, string fairy lights behind the actors and keep them out of focus; a phone's portrait mode or simply standing far from the background is enough. Play quiet music only between takes and add it in the edit, so the dialogue stays clean. Film Reyes's phone lines separately and play them under Jay's close-up. The street scene works at any kerb with a street light; record a wild track of traffic so you can smooth the cuts. Do several takes of the coin moment so the coin lands cleanly.

ul: Jay barely reacts to the mockery. He is a man finishing a test, not a victim; dry and polite is stronger than hurt.
Marcus should enjoy himself enormously. The bigger his confidence, the funnier and more satisfying his collapse.
Sophie is not a villain. Her line about wanting it enough is said with real disappointment, which makes Jay's reply sting.
Hold the silence after Marcus says he is standing right here. Let the guests lower their phones one by one.
Reyes speaks fast and flat, like someone reading a schedule. The calmer she sounds, the bigger the news feels.
Common mistake: making Jay gloat. He gives the coin back gently; the face-slap lands because he does not need it.
Move the party to a wedding reception or a school reunion in a rented hall, with Jay delivering the cake.
Swap genders: a female rider delivers to her ex-boyfriend's engagement party, and his new fiancée mocks her.
Change the ending: the second heir in the will is Marcus, which means Jay and Marcus are cousins and have to work together.

faq.q: Can I post my version on a monetised channel or a drama app?
faq.a: Yes. The script is CC BY 4.0, so commercial use is allowed. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the description or the closing card.

faq.q: Do I need a real luxury venue?
faq.a: No. A living room with fairy lights, a few friends in their best clothes and a table of drinks reads as a party on a phone screen. Keep the frame tight and the background soft.

faq.q: Why is Sophie named in the will?
faq.a: Episode 1 leaves it open on purpose. Jay's grandfather may have known Sophie, tested her too, or wanted the two of them to run things together; pick the answer that gives your episode 2 the best conflict.
